leftEvidence.title: Moses appeals to the LORD’s name and reputation among the nations

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Moses argues that Egypt and the land’s inhabitants know the LORD is present with Israel and will hear if Israel is killed together.
points.right: The prayer recalls bread, water, a command to possess the land, proud refusal, and a desire to return to bondage.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: He asks for the LORD’s power to be great according to the proclaimed character that forgives yet does not clear guilt.
points.right: God is remembered as ready to pardon, merciful, and sustaining the people forty years despite rebellion.

payload.posture: Moses appeals to the LORD’s proclaimed character, and Nehemiah later remembers God as ready to pardon and sustaining in the wilderness.

rightEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
rightEvidence.title: A later prayer remembers refusal alongside continued mercy

payload.tension: Nehemiah selects mercy and provision without reproducing the generation sentence in full.
payload.title: Intercession and remembered pardon
